practicality.justification: The recommendation is straightforward for a small operator: test one offer, set an exact $85 threshold, and run a 50/50 A/B test with a clear profit-per-session formula. It is deployable with basic e-commerce tools, but the 30-day plan lacks operational details such as traffic allocation mechanics, sample size, or how to display the offer.
quotes: Run a 50/50 A/B test for 30 days where half your traffic gets the standard experience and half gets the $85 free shipping offer.
practicality.improvement: Add minimum sample size/power requirements, specify how the free-shipping banner/cart messaging will be implemented, and include a monitoring cadence during the 30 days.

specificity.justification: The answer uses the supplied economics to propose an exact threshold ($85), explains the 18% uplift calculation, quantifies the 15% discount as $10.80, estimates margin contribution from the added item, and provides a concrete gross-profit-per-session formula and decision rule.
quotes: Set your offer to: "Free Shipping on Orders Over $85"
( (Total Revenue x 0.42) - (Number of Free Shipping Orders x $9) ) / Total Sessions
specificity.improvement: Add a pre-test break-even calculation for required AOV or conversion lift and define a minimum detectable profit difference with a statistical confidence threshold.

risk_awareness.justification: The candidate notes a margin tradeoff by comparing the $9 shipping subsidy to the $10.80 discount hit and argues free shipping is mathematically safer, but it does not identify customer behavior risks such as threshold gaming or low-AOV segment effects, nor experiment-design risks such as sample size, novelty effect, seasonality, or contamination. It also does not explain controls beyond a simple profit comparison.
quotes: absorbing a $9 shipping cost on a higher order value is mathematically safer for your margins than taking a straight $10.80 hit
At a 42% margin, that extra $15 item generates $6.30 in gross profit, heavily offsetting the $9 shipping cost you are now absorbing.
risk_awareness.improvement: State the break-even lift required, define guardrails like minimum margin per order, specify statistical significance/sample size and test duration controls, segment new vs returning visitors, and monitor shipping cost variance and threshold-gaming behavior.

overall_impression: A strong, specific, and practical starting recommendation with an exact threshold and profit-focused metric, but it underplays experiment-design and customer-behavior risks and lacks statistical rigor.
